Posted September 29, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.

For the second time in two weeks, a major concession by the DEAland prohibitionist establishment may have a significant impact on Canadians. Last week, John Walters declined to oppose Chicago's move toward decrim.
See
 Decrim Okay With Drug Czar Walters? A Gaffe or a Miracle? Lessons for Canada.They Should Also Notice Alaska.

(So far, the Canadian media have not recognized the significance of this retreat for the coming debate in Ottawa on Prime Minister Martin's phony decrim bill.)

Now, the DEA has finally given up on its power grab to ban any foods that might contain even minute traces of THC. (This victory will not come as a surprise to MarijuanaNews readers.)
See
 Victory for Hemp Shows Prohibitionist Have Problems With Mandatory Stupidity. The Prohibitionist Dilemma Is That They Are Addicted to Bad Arguments.
and links

However, the ban on hemp cultivation in DEAland will remain in place, so Canadian farmers will be the most likely suppliers for high quality hemp seeds and oil.
See
 CBS Eye On America Let's Drug Czar Barry McCaffrey Make a Fool Of Himself About Hemp Cultivation

Although, the outcome seemed obvious for some time, the three year battle made it very difficult to do long-term planning on hemp production in Canada. A look back in the Hemp archives on MarijuanaNews shows that, four or five years ago, there was still much optimism about growing and processing hemp products for the huge US health food markets as well as for hemp fabrics.

Introducing new crops is always a slow process, and the learning curve for hemp cultivation suffered from the plant having been excluded from the last fifty years of agricultural research.

The nascent Canadian hemp industry had the usual problems inherent in any new product, but the biggest problem turned out to be the DEA's effort to ban hemp foods. That was a risk factor that investors were understandably unwilling to confront. Now they are free to invest in production and research, and face only the normal business risks.

David Bronner, president of Dr. Bronner's Magic Soaps, which makes hemp oil based soaps and other products, including an energy bar, reportedly spent $200,000 fighting for everyone's freedom. (David is a remarkable person, and I hope that everyone will show their appreciation by buying Bronner's products.)

Because hemp has many unique nutritional properties, and a huge potential as a source for nutriceuticals, the way is now open for the development of new products and markets. This victory will also be a source of comfort for those who depend on hemp foods and hemp seed oil for health maintenance. (This is a much larger group than most people realize.)

Politically, this is very important because it means that hemp will be more and more visible in health food stores which are patronized by highly educated people, and the huge health food industry is very influential in Washington.

This exposure was the DEA's real concern. The reefer madness crowd is the hardcore constituency of the Drug War, and for them the demonization of cannabis is paramount. Having the hemp leaf portrayed as a source of anything good will greatly aggravate their rabies.
